full_judgment:
4. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing the parties found that the suit was in substance for setting aside the award dated 5.8.79 and since the cause of action in the suit according to the plaintiff arose on 7.12.79 when the plaintiff came to know about the award for the first time and since the plaintiff as defendant No.2 appeared in Title Suit No. 366 of 1978 on 20.12.79 and since the present suit was instituted on 5.12.81 the suit was barred under the provisions of Article 158 of the Limitation Act. The learned Subordinate Judge after holding that the suit was barred by limitation rejected the plaint under Order 7 rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. It is submitted by Mr. Dewan AMS Zaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff appellant, that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in holding that the suit was barred under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. The learned Advocate, however, submitted that the period of limitation for such suit was 6 years under Article 120 of the Limitation Act. But on the perusal of the application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is apparent that the defendant-petitioners filed the application praying for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit was barred under the provisions of the Arbitration Act, 1940. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge went beyond the pleadings and wrongly held that the suit was barred by Article 158 of the Limitation Act. The question before the Court was whether the suit was barred by law as provided in clause (d) of rule 11 of Order 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. From the reading of the plaint it does not appear that the suit was barred by limitation. The learned Subordinate Judge, therefore, was wrong in holding that the plaint was liable to be rejected as the suit was barred by limitation under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. 

 It appears that sub-section (2) of section 31 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for time being in force, all questions regarding the validity of an award shall be decided by the Court in which the award has been filed or may be filed and by no other Court. Section 32 gives the scheme of the Arbitration Act which is to prevent the parties to the arbitration agreement from agitating the question relating to arbitration in any manner other than that provided by the Act and it prohibits the filing of a suit for setting aside, amending or modifying in any wayan award. Sections 31 and 32 of the Arbitration Act bar any suit to set aside an award otherwise than as provided in the Arbitration Act itself and section 33 provides the remedy to the parties who desire to challenge the validity of an arbitration agreement or the award itself. It is under section 33 that any party to an arbitration agreement may apply to the Court for setting aside the award on the grounds as provided in section 30 of the Arbitration Act. The period of 30 days limitation provided under Article 158 of the Limitation Act is applicable to such an application for setting aside an award and the limitation starts from the date of service of notice of filing of the award in Court. 

 10. In the case before us the plaintiff-appellant filed the suit for a declaration that the award dated 5.8.79 which was filed in Court in Title Suit No. 366 of 1977 was illegal void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The defendants thereafter filed the application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit was barred by the provisions of Arbitration Act. Since section 32 of the Arbitration Act bars such a suit challenging the validity of an award we find that the suit was barred by the provision of section 32 of the Arbitration Act. The learned Subordinate Judge should have rejected the plaint on the finding that it was barred by the provision of section 32 of the Arbitration Act. Instead he rejected the plaint as being barred under Article 158 of the Limitation Act which is not tenable.
